added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: blocking: The synthetic A and B recorded-axis spline gradients are 2.433e-4 and 2.638e-4 against the required rounding-level 1e-9 check; the field reconstruction is therefore unqualified for those records under done-when clause 1.

blocking: Adapter B polishes record-seeded and grid-bracketed stationary points and chooses the nearest result; its flux is computed from that result, so saying the exact imas-efit level match is by construction misstates the central provenance question, and the synthetic export levels differ by 1.19e-9 and 1.40e-9.

blocking: The 22 psi contour levels are generated per record from the grid range but neither page.py:258 nor the figure labels state those levels, leaving an explicit poloidal-panel requirement unmet.

follow-on: Saddle distance uses imas-efit's source grid node as the coordinate but pairs it with the refined saddle level; the summary labels that proxy as saddle distance without telling the reader it is a source-node distance.

follow-on: The negative-control assertion calls require_rebuild directly, so a regression that removes rebuild_table's call to that guard would still leave this test green while the page reports failed records as passing.
follow-on: The reviewed run records a head test log but no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so added_failure_count cannot be measured from paired gate logs and must remain null.

item_verdicts.diff: I read all nine commits from 1b25eedd7574fda2220c02fc33fffd39db9433bd through 8542624b7e01a962c4e7149c23fe632ae9f39aa2; scripts/prototypes/efit_axis_adjudication/test_rebuild.py:46 adds a negative assertion and the later page and plot commits repair the earlier omissions.
item_verdicts.done_when: The five clauses in the source brief are partly evidenced by docs/research/efit-axis-adjudication.html:80-81 and out/results.json; the two synthetic gradients exceed 1e-9, and plot.py:123 draws psi contours without stating their levels in the page.
item_verdicts.goal: The source brief requests neutral plots and tables for the lead; docs/research/efit-axis-adjudication.html:54-89 carries 26 records and five figures, but its synthetic rebuilds fail and its adapter B provenance claim is too strong.
item_verdicts.manifest: The source manifest.md:15 records a passing focused rebuild test and names its log, but it has no baseline_suite or after_suite arms from which to measure added failures.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The brief grants scripts/prototypes/efit_axis_adjudication, the figure directory, the research page and the evidence fragment; the base-to-head diff changes only those four path families.

justifications.durability: test_rebuild.py:21-23 fails if its page module cannot load, and its line 46 fails if require_rebuild accepts either synthetic axis or raises another error, as the tolerance mutation demonstrates; it never tests the generated page's fail label.
justifications.evidence: test_rebuild.py:46 has a head gate and a red tolerance mutation in out/rebuild-negative-final.log, but the source manifest.md:15 supplies no comparable baseline and after suite arms.
justifications.fit: plot.py:21 reuses nova.media.poloidal.draw_nulls and line 45 sets a common 14-inch canvas with text checks, while plot.py:123 leaves the contour levels unstated in the delivered captions.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/research/efit-axis-adjudication.html:80-81 openly reports two failed rebuilds, while page.py:315-318 incorrectly presents adapter B's independently polished result as an exact match by construction.
justifications.reuse: A capability search found scripts/prototypes/read_robustness/census.py:26 for a Bell-field census and nova/equilibrium/flux_surface_geometry.py:427 for spline interpolation, while field.py:17 and census.py:78 serve the independently required trace-spline analysis and plot.py:21 reuses the existing null glyph owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: The base-to-head diff confines all changes to the brief's four path families, including scripts/prototypes/efit_axis_adjudication/analyse.py and docs/research/efit-axis-adjudication.html.
